summary: Quarterly renewal / expansion check-in. Arcadia is approaching contract renewal in mid-July and want to expand capacity and add an EU region for lower latency to European clinics. transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-06-14; Start 15:00 UTC; Duration ~45 min
Attendees: Sam Pierce (Redwood AE), Riya Khatri (Redwood SE), Liam O'Connor (Redwood CSM), Michael Chen (CTO, Arcadia), Priya Patel (Head MLOps), Sara Kim (SRE), Dave Lopez (Procurement)

Summary: Quick check-in to align on renewal timeline, discuss expansion to EU region, and sizing for additional dedicated capacity. Short tech deep-dive on expected throughput and failover behavior.

00:00 Sam Pierce: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intro — Sam from Redwood, joined by Riya and Liam. how's everyone?
00:12 Michael Chen: Hey Sam, doing well. we've been busy with the spring rollout. main thing for today is renewal and EU region, and want to understand costs and SLOs.
00:27 Sam Pierce: Great. quick context: your contract ends mid-July, right? we penciled you for a renewal conversation. can you confirm target timeline and any internal deadlines?
00:38 Priya Patel: yes mid-July. procurement window is narrow, ideally have committed pricing and paperwork by end of June. also we need EU datacenter for patient-facing latency.
00:51 Riya Khatri: On the EU side, we can deploy Private or Dedicated in eu-west with same API surface. It’s usually a choice between expanding Dedicated capacity (reserved GPUs) or enabling multi-region routing with burst across hosted pools. both have trade offs.
01:05 Sara Kim: security wise we need SOC2 attestations, SAML SSO, and KMS integration for keys. is that all supported for multi-region?
01:15 Riya Khatri: Yes, we support those for Dedicated and Private deployments. note: audit logs are available across regions; you can centralize to your SIEM. minor caveat is private control plane for on-prem needs extra lead time.
01:30 Michael Chen: Cost question — what's the delta for adding EU region and for committed GPUs?
01:35 Sam Pierce: typical delta: adding a region is an add-on monthly fee plus committed capacity price for the reserved GPUs. for a 12-month commit we can give a discount tier — i'll put numbers in the quote. example: 4x A100-equivalent for dedicated baseline, and burst to hosted for spikes.
01:52 Priya Patel: we're trying to keep avg latency under 150ms for inference to European clinics — do you have benchmarks?
01:58 Riya Khatri: we do. i'll share the eu-west latency report we ran for a similar health customer. note that the KV cache warmup and prefix caching behavior helps keep tail latency down. sometimes the transcription shows KV "cash" in earlier notes, sorry for that.
02:18 Michael Chen: also procurement will need SLA numbers — p99, p95.
02:22 Sam Pierce: our Dedicated SLAs can be attached. p95 and p99 latency targets depend on model and sequences, we can scope with a short benchmark.
02:32 Dave Lopez: on procurement — what's required for PO and is there a minimum commit?
02:36 Sam Pierce: minimum commit typically a monthly committed GPU equivalent, for enterprise we do flexible tiers. i'll detail PO process in the quote; we can include billing cadence options.
02:45 Priya Patel: any competitors to worry about? management asked if Vertex or Sagemaker could be cheaper.
02:50 Sam Pierce: yep teams evaluate Google Vertex and AWS SageMaker. main differences: Redwood focuses on production inference economics — caching, batching, and model routing — to reduce per token cost. sometimes the comparison misses that hosted burst behavior and KV cache can change unit costs.
03:10 Riya Khatri: small tech note: If you increase dedicated pool size you get better stable latency and easier isolation for PHI. If you rely on hosted burst, you may see small variance during heavy spikes.
03:25 Michael Chen: for the pilot in EU we want 2 dedicated nodes for a week to validate latency and throughput, then decide commit size.
03:33 Sam Pierce: good. we can spin that up — Riya will run benchmark runbook with your team.
03:40 Riya Khatri: i'll need sample workload, typical qps, sequence lengths, and which model variants you use (we saw you on redwood-llama-13b earlier but it's fine to confirm). note: model names in some internal docs were mis-typed as 'redwood dediate' — ignore that.
03:58 Priya Patel: current throughput is ~40 qps avg daytime, peaks ~120 qps. sequence length average 256 tokens.
04:08 Riya Khatri: with those numbers we recommend starting with 4 GPU equivalent reserved capacity in EU for stable 150ms p95 for the 13b family, and scale to 8 for heavy peaks, or use burst config. we'll write exact numbers in the runbook.
04:25 Michael Chen: security — can you confirm audit logs retention and KMS options? we need 7 years retention for some events.
04:34 Liam O'Connor: yes audit logs can be exported to your cloud storage/ SIEM; retention is configurable via the console if you're on enterprise plan, otherwise we can provide long-term export via support. KMS/HSM integrations supported with customer-managed keys.
04:52 Dave Lopez: any paperwork we should start now?
04:55 Sam Pierce: i'll include terms and a template amendment for the extension to 12 months and for region add-on. also include pricing tiers and cancellation clauses.
05:05 Priya Patel: one more — can we test data residency for EU, make sure no tokens are routed back to us-east?
05:11 Riya Khatri: yes, we can lock routing so requests from EU endpoints stay in the EU region and failover to nearby region only if configured. we'll include routing policy suggestions.
05:22 Michael Chen: ok sounds good.
05:25 Sam Pierce: recap — Sam will send quote and PO template, Riya will send benchmark doc and eu latency report, Priya will confirm stakeholders, Dave starts procurement timeline. we'll target to have commitments by 6/21 to hit procurement window.
05:40 Michael Chen: thanks everyone, appreciate it.

End of transcript.

Notes: occasional transcription artifacts: 'redwood dediate' for Dedicated, 'KV cash' instead of KV cache, 'Anthropec' mis-heard for Anthropic in quick mentions.
